headline: Leasing momentum builds while property-sale gains normalize
summary_short: Brixmor's Q2 2026 revenue rose 4.3% y/y to $354.2M as billed occupancy climbed to 90.4% and blended re-leasing spreads held at 13.6%, but net income fell to $73.5M ($0.24 diluted EPS) from $127.8M in Q1 2026 on a much smaller property-disposition gain.
summary_long: Revenue grew 4.3% y/y to $354.2M on contractual rent increases, positive re-leasing spreads (13.6% blended) and higher billed occupancy (90.4% vs 89.7% y/y). Net income fell 13.7% y/y and 42.5% q/q to $73.5M ($0.24 diluted EPS) as this quarter's $9.8M gain on property sales was far smaller than Q1's larger disposition gain, and $6.0M of real estate was impaired. Same-property NOI rose 5.8% y/y; Nareit FFO per diluted share rose to $0.58 from $0.56. Cash fell to $170.9M on $600M of note repayments versus $398.5M of new note issuance; long-term debt eased to $5,322.4M. No numeric FY2026 guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Core leasing fundamentals improved (occupancy up, positive re-leasing spreads, same-property NOI growth), but GAAP net income and FFO-adjacent q/q comparisons were dragged down by a much smaller property-disposition gain than Q1 2026 plus a $6.0M impairment.

Base rent grew from contractual escalations and positive re-leasing spreads on new/renewal/option leases, plus higher billed occupancy; partly offset by lower straight-line rent and below-market lease accretion.
Tracks revenue growth outpacing a smaller rise in operating costs and real estate taxes (higher repairs/maintenance/utilities/insurance and property assessments).
Revenue growth and lower G&A (down on lower net compensation costs) were partly offset by higher depreciation/amortization from transaction activity and a $6.0M impairment on one property.

This quarter's $9.8M gain on sale of real estate was far smaller than Q1 2026's implied $52.1M gain (derived: six-months-2026 total gain of $61.9M less this quarter's $9.8M), and interest expense rose on higher weighted average debt and rates.
Tracks the lower net income; weighted average basic shares were roughly flat q/q and y/y, so the EPS decline mirrors the net income decline almost directly.
Tracks the same smaller disposition-gain and impairment dynamics behind the net income decline against a roughly flat revenue base.
Cash fell q/q as $600.0M of unsecured notes were repaid against $398.5M of new unsecured notes issued in May 2026, plus $191.4M of stockholder distributions and $123.5M of reinvestment capex.
Net debt eased q/q as the $600.0M note repayment exceeded the $398.5M of new unsecured notes issued in May 2026 (proceeds used partly to fund the terminated interest-rate lock agreements).
Modest q/q decline as $0.3075/share of declared common dividends exceeded the quarter's $73.5M net income contribution to retained earnings.
